title: Learning Expressive and Compositional Motion Representation via Spectral Skills
abstract: arXiv:2609.37677v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robotic foundation models offer a promising path toward general-purpose humanoid robot control, often through hierarchical architectures. However, their effectiveness depends on the command interface between the planner and the controller, which must support accurate execution while remaining easy to predict, and ideally allow new behaviors to be composed from prior ones. In this work, we introduce spectral skills, a latent representation of this interface that meets these requirements through predictive representation learning. By design, spectral skills compactly encode short motion segments and are learned by predicting subsequent motion rather than reconstructing the encoder input. On a 29-DoF humanoid, a controller conditioned on spectral skills reduces global tracking error by 62\% relative to the state of the art. translated_title: 通过谱技能学习富有表现力且可组合的运动表示
translated_abstract: 机器人基础模型为通用人形机器人控制提供了一条有前景的路径，通常通过分层架构来实现。然而，其有效性取决于规划器与控制器之间的命令接口，该接口必须支持精确执行，同时保持易于预测，并理想地能够从已有行为组合出新的行为。在这项工作中，我们提出了谱技能，这是一种通过预测性表示学习满足上述要求的接口潜在表示。通过设计，谱技能紧凑地编码短运动片段，并通过预测后续运动而非重构编码器输入来进行学习。在29自由度人形机器人上，以谱技能为条件的控制器相对于现有技术将全局跟踪误差降低了62%。同一个冻结的控制器无需单独的过渡策略即可链接独立编码的技能，它还可以组合……
tldr: 提出谱技能这一基于预测性表示学习的潜在运动表示接口，使29自由度人形机器人的控制器跟踪误差降低62%，并支持冻结控制器对独立编码技能的链式组合。
en_tdlr: Proposes spectral skills, a latent motion interface learned via predictive representation learning, which reduces tracking error by 62% on a 29-DoF humanoid and enables a frozen controller to chain and compose independently encoded skills.
